clue.text: Tricky situation, having to preserve a mischievous child

definitions.meaning: a jam or fix, an awkward predicament one is in
to keep vegetables in vinegar or brine
an informal British name for a naughty little rascal

explanation.surface: A parent in a fix, forced to keep an eye on a naughty youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together, joined by 'having to'. Calling an impish child a 'little pickle' is everyday British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word covers a predicament, the act of preserving in vinegar, and a cheeky youngster.

clue.text: Staff around but it needs filling

indicators.note: the staff goes round the word for but

parts.note: a pole is a staff or rod
tho is an informal spelling of though, meaning but

explanation.surface: A stick wrapped round something that still needs to be filled.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a road surface is something the council must fill in.

clue.text: Catholic penetrating spy organisation, getting about

indicators.note: the Catholic abbreviation gets inside the spy agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
RC is short for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A Catholic infiltrates the US spy agency and gets around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word placed before a date to mean approximately.

clue.text: Child in stories that's not saying enough

indicators.note: the small child goes inside the stories

parts.note: lies are untrue stories
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child caught in a tissue of untruths that falls short of the full account.
explanation.definitionFit: Understatement by negating the opposite, like 'not bad', says less than is meant.

clue.text: Dull Second and Third from Prokofiev, ending in Vaughan Williams' mortified cry?

parts.note: matt, also spelt mat, describes a dull surface without shine

indicators.note: only the second and third letters of the composer's name are kept, the rest dropped
the final letter of the word Vaughan is taken

explanation.surface: A music critic picks out the dreary second and third movements of a Prokofiev piece and then a gloomy Vaughan Williams finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaughan Williams' looks like one composer, but the clue splits him: N comes from 'Vaughan', and 'Williams' is Kenneth Williams, the British Carry On film comic whose catchphrase was an outraged 'Ooh, Matron!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital's senior nurse is the figure Kenneth Williams famously wailed at in the Carry On films.

clue.text: A poet entertaining circle on a ship

indicators.note: the poet hosts the circle inside himself

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O is a circle shape

explanation.surface: A poet amusing a group of friends during a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on board a vessel or vehicle means you are on it.

clue.text: Feel low, as every daughter in line heading for nuptials

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the row

parts.note: a row is a line
each means every one

indicators.note: the first letter of nuptials is taken

explanation.surface: A father feels down as each daughter lines up for her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch a hand downwards is to feel about at a low level.

clue.text: Publication for whom monkey writes cryptic

indicators.note: the letters of monkey writes are shuffled into something puzzling

explanation.surface: A paper whose crossword is supposedly written by a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A playful self-dig: Paul, the setter, also writes crosswords for this American paper.
explanation.definitionFit: This American daily newspaper is a well-known publication.

clue.text: Brunette with plait plaited, sweet thing

indicators.note: the letters of brunette and plait are woven together like braided hair

explanation.surface: A dark-haired woman with her hair braided is a lovely person.
explanation.definitionFit: A brittle confection of nuts set in hard caramel is a sweet.

clue.text: See 26
Popular figure into reforming, yet law unto herself, the Queen

indicators.note: the admired figure is placed inside the rearranged letters
the words yet law are being formed anew, so their letters are shuffled

parts.note: a hero is someone widely admired

explanation.surface: A celebrity joins a reform movement, though the monarch remains a law unto herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular figure' looks like part of the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is how the monarch speaks of herself.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural pronoun a monarch traditionally uses in place of 'I' when speaking of herself.

clue.text: Old 26 9, lightweight in store

indicators.note: the small weight sits inside the shop

parts.note: a mart is a market or shop
oz, an ounce, is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A has-been celebrity, a featherweight, turns up in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old 26 9' points to 26 and 9 together, MEGASTAR: an old megastar, here the eighteenth-century composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer was a celebrated superstar of classical music who died long ago.

clue.text: Bearing right, work to see name on old US aircraft

parts.note: north is a compass direction or bearing
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A navigator takes a bearing, turns right and gets to work spotting a name painted on a vintage American plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northrop company built many American military planes, so its name appears on their fuselages.

clue.text: So brevity different!

indicators.note: the letters of the words so brevity are made different by rearranging them

explanation.surface: An exclamation contrasting wordiness with terseness.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordiness is precisely what differs from being brief, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Pubs' motto, possibly?

indicators.note: the letters of pubs motto might possibly be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A guess at what a pub might have as its slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Pubs'' gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The drinkers' toast urging everyone to drain their glasses is a fitting slogan for a pub.

clue.text: Weak film about boxing

definitions.meaning: unsteady or shaky, as in a wobbly position
the 1976 Sylvester Stallone movie about a fighter from Philadelphia

explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and unstable describes something weak, and the Stallone boxing movie bears the same title.

clue.text: Strike small arachnid

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mite is a tiny eight-legged creature related to spiders

explanation.surface: Swatting a tiny spider-like bug.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit hard, an old-fashioned or biblical word for a blow.

clue.text: Paul's set up drink, then game wrapped in fruit, but no starter for 26 9

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so Paul's means Paul is, I'm
cha is tea

indicators.note: the game is enclosed by the fruit
the first letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
jacks is a children's game of tossing small pieces

explanation.surface: The setter knocks back a drink and plays a game wrapped in fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 9 is MEGASTAR. 'Paul's' works because Paul is the setter, and 'set up' reverses upwards because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The King of Pop was one of the biggest celebrities in the world.

clue.text: Little time to cry, protecting wife after a month in siege

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: the cry wraps around the following pieces as though guarding them

parts.note: a roar is a loud cry

indicators.note: the wife's letter comes after the month

parts.note: Jan is short for January

explanation.surface: Someone briefly cries out, sheltering his wife during a month-long siege.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the standard abbreviation for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary ten-year war centred on the Greek siege of the city of Troy.

clue.text: See 17
Welshman's grasped member, it's claimed

indicators.note: the Welshman holds the limb inside

parts.note: Aled is a Welsh man's name, as in the singer Aled Jones
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Welshman has grabbed someone's leg, or so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said to be so but not proven is supposedly true.

clue.text: 26 9, model no more

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters of no more are reshaped

explanation.surface: A star, once a model, now finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 9 is MEGASTAR: Marilyn, who began as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn was one of Hollywood's biggest stars of the 1950s.

clue.text: Empty hen house duck found centrally in street

indicators.note: the poultry pieces sit inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a coop is a hutch for poultry
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

indicators.note: the central letter of the word found is taken

explanation.surface: A farmer discovers a hen house with a duck sitting in the middle of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To hollow something out by digging away its contents, as with a spoon.

clue.text: Farm animals talked regularly behind domestic animal

indicators.note: the alternate letters follow the pet

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet

indicators.note: every other letter of the word talked is taken

explanation.surface: Farm creatures chattering away, following the household pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows, bulls and oxen kept on a farm are collectively known by this word.

clue.text: See 7
Patient accommodating seconds, parts to find hot meals

indicators.note: the patient takes in the abbreviation for seconds

parts.note: a doctor refers to a patient as a case
roles are parts played by actors

explanation.surface: A hospital patient with an appetite for second helpings finds parts of hot dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: Stews cooked slowly in an oven dish are hot meals of this kind.

clue.text: Both thin and thick stuff written by me — quite some name!

indicators.note: the substances are placed after the word me, as though written beside it

parts.note: taken as written
gas is thin vapour
tar is thick black sticky material

explanation.surface: A writer boasts of producing both light and heavy material, making a big name for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both' signals that the phrase supplies two things: GAS for the thin stuff, TAR for the thick.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely famous celebrity is someone with a very big name indeed.

clue.text: Invalid guided around a rider

indicators.note: the guiding word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: led means guided
a PS, postscript, is a rider added to a letter

explanation.surface: An invalid is steered round by someone on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a sick person, but it is the adjective meaning no longer in force.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy or membership that has expired is no longer valid.

clue.text: New beginnings in double entendres, Uranus circling 9 being taken from behind

indicators.note: the whole string is read from the back to the front
the opening letters of the words double and entendres are taken

parts.note: 9 across is star, and the sun is a star
the planet Uranus, U, orbits the sun and so comes beside it

explanation.surface: Fresh material: smutty jokes about a planet circling a star, mocking the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken from behind' turns DESUNU around, a cheeky nod to the familiar Uranus joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never used is still new, in mint condition.
